name: Quip
tagline: Salesforce's collaborative docs and spreadsheets platform
description: The main Quip alternatives are Google Docs and Sheets, Microsoft 365 with Loop, Notion, Confluence and Coda for shared documents, and Slack canvases if your team already lives in Slack. GAIA is a different kind of alternative: an AI assistant that cuts the work around documents by turning email, meetings and tasks into finished actions across your tools.
metaTitle: Quip Alternatives: Quip vs GAIA for Docs, Salesforce and AI
metaDescription: Quip keeps docs and chat inside Salesforce. GAIA triages email, manages tasks, and runs workflows across your tools. Compare pricing.
intro:
Quip is Salesforce's collaborative documents and spreadsheets product. It started independently, was acquired by Salesforce in 2016, and is now built around Salesforce CRM: sales teams embed live Salesforce records and lists in documents, attach Quip docs to account and opportunity pages, and co-edit account plans with comments and chat beside the text. That tie to Salesforce is its main reason to exist, and it is also why people look for something else once they leave Salesforce or need a broader tool.

Quip competitors, by what you need. For everyday co-editing of docs and spreadsheets: Google Docs and Sheets, or Microsoft Word, Excel and Loop if you run on Microsoft 365. For a team wiki and project docs: Notion or Confluence. For docs that behave like apps (tables, buttons, automations): Coda. For quick shared docs inside chat: Slack canvases. If you stay on Salesforce and only need deal documents with live CRM data, Quip remains the most direct fit.

Quip vs Slack for teams on Salesforce: both are Salesforce products, and they solve different problems. Quip is document-first: a long account plan or a spreadsheet with comments and a chat thread attached. Slack is conversation-first: channels, threads and huddles, with canvases for lighter documents and Salesforce apps that bring records into channels. If your team writes long, structured documents tied to CRM records, Quip fits. If most coordination happens in conversation and documents are short, Slack with canvases covers it and you run one tool instead of two.

GAIA is built for a different model. Instead of a better shared document, it is a proactive AI assistant across your workflow. It reads your Gmail inbox and creates tasks, calendar events and action items. It works with Slack, GitHub, Linear, Jira, Notion, Todoist, Google Docs and other tools rather than one CRM vendor's ecosystem, and its memory keeps track of the people, projects and decisions you share with it across conversations. GAIA has no co-editing editor and no Salesforce integration, so it replaces the follow-up work around documents, not the documents themselves.

verdict: Choose Quip if your organization runs on Salesforce and needs account planning documents with live CRM data embedded. Choose Google Docs, Microsoft 365, Notion, Confluence or Coda if you need a strong shared editor outside Salesforce. Choose GAIA if the real cost is the work around documents (email, meetings, tasks and follow-ups across a broad set of tools), with source-available flexibility.

faqs.question: Is GAIA a good Quip alternative for non-Salesforce teams?
faqs.answer: Yes, if what you need is the work around documents rather than the editor itself. Quip's main value is its Salesforce integration, which makes it less compelling for teams not on Salesforce. GAIA offers proactive automation, email management and task tracking across common developer and productivity tools. For co-editing, pair it with Google Docs or Notion, which GAIA can also work with.

faqs.question: Does GAIA integrate with Salesforce?
faqs.answer: No. GAIA does not have a Salesforce CRM integration. Its integrations include Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack, GitHub, Linear, Jira, Notion, Todoist and HubSpot, among others, and you can add custom MCP servers. Teams whose core workflow centers on Salesforce records should check whether that covers their needs.

faqs.question: How does GAIA handle collaborative document editing compared to Quip?
faqs.answer: Quip is purpose-built for real-time collaborative document and spreadsheet editing with embedded comments and chat. GAIA's strength is AI-driven orchestration and workflow automation rather than a rich collaborative editor. Teams that rely heavily on co-editing long documents will find Quip's editor more suited to that specific task.

faqs.question: Is GAIA cheaper than Quip?
faqs.answer: Quip is typically priced as part of enterprise Salesforce licensing. GAIA's hosted Pro plan is ${{PRO_MONTHLY_PRICE}}/month, and self-hosting is free for non-commercial use (plus your own model API costs).

faqs.question: Can GAIA handle sales team workflows?
faqs.answer: GAIA can help with email follow-ups, meeting preparation, task tracking and workflow automation that matter in sales work. It does not offer CRM features like deal pipelines, contact records or account hierarchies, so it suits individual productivity and cross-tool coordination better than pipeline management.

faqs.question: What are the best Quip alternatives?
faqs.answer: It depends on what you use Quip for. For co-editing docs and spreadsheets: Google Docs and Sheets, or Microsoft 365 with Loop. For a team wiki: Notion or Confluence. For app-like docs: Coda. For short docs inside chat: Slack canvases. To cut the follow-up work around documents (emails, meetings, tasks), add an assistant like GAIA.

faqs.question: Quip vs Slack: which is better for Salesforce teams?
faqs.answer: Quip, for long and structured documents tied to Salesforce records, such as account plans, with comments and chat beside the text. Slack, for day-to-day coordination in channels and threads, with canvases for short documents and Salesforce apps that surface records in Slack. Salesforce teams that mostly talk rather than write often find Slack alone is enough.

faqs.question: What does Quip integrate with?
faqs.answer: Mainly Salesforce: live records and list views inside documents, and Quip documents on Salesforce record pages. It also offers Live Apps (embedded components such as calendars, kanban boards and project trackers) and a Slack integration for sharing documents and notifications. Outside that, its third-party ecosystem is smaller than Google Workspace, Microsoft 365 or Notion.
